title: Warhawk
subtitle: A battlefield shared between the ground and sky

body: Warhawk is Incognito Entertainment's PlayStation 3 multiplayer action game, first released in North America on 28 August 2007. Soldiers, vehicles and aircraft fight over large maps, allowing the player to change roles within the same battle. A person defending an objective on foot can later take a vehicle or climb into a Warhawk to influence the fight from above. The different scales connect rather than occupy separate games. A threat in the sky matters to the people below, while a position captured on the ground can change what the surrounding battle allows.

Deathmatch, team battles, Zones and Capture the Flag give the same maps different objectives. The player has to read both the immediate opposition and the larger situation: another aircraft may be a useful target, but a ground position can be more important to the result. Map configurations vary the space and conditions, encouraging different approaches to familiar terrain. Progress unlocks personnel and aircraft customisation, giving continued play another visible reward. The main attraction remains the ability to move between kinds of combat as the needs of the match change.

Warhawk became the first PlayStation 3 release available both as a physical product and a PlayStation Network download. A planned single-player component was removed so development could concentrate on multiplayer. Dylan Jobe directed, with Christopher Lennertz and Timothy Michael Wynn composing the music. Updates addressed early technical issues and added further modes, while expansions supplied maps and equipment. Its later spiritual successor, Starhawk, continued the interest in a shared battlefield. Warhawk's original achievement was to make changing from a soldier to a pilot feel like a decision inside one continuing contest.
